title: Scurraway / Josiah's Neck
summary: Scurraway is recorded as the Native name of Josiah's Neck in Babylon, east of Amityville.
history_content: Scurraway was one of the three necks purchased in 1658, although it was not named in that first record. A 1697 Huntington record identifies the land as Scuraway in Native usage and Josiah's Neck in English.
translation_content:
The name probably means "snake place," though the source also leaves open the possibility that it was the name of a Native person living there.

Why Place Names Matter

“When you understand the names, you begin to understand the stories. And that changes how you see the world.”

— Melinda Quintero, Place Names, Narratives, and Mapping Reconciliation (2024), featured quotation
preservation_content: Scurraway preserves an older name for a south-shore neck later remembered in English as Josiah's Neck, showing how Native and colonial names overlapped in meadow and shoreline records.
